name: Slide Deck from Content
description:
Turn a body of source content into a presentation deck. Outlines the narrative first, designs a consistent slide look, then builds the deck (HTML slides), evaluating for narrative flow and visual consistency.

A gallery craftbook generated from an archetype spec. It runs
`phase → (per-phase gate) → … → evaluate → (loop) → finish`. Each build
phase that produces a checkable artifact is followed by a **runtime
gate-checkpoint** — the runtime verifies the artifact and routes with no
model turn, looping back to redo the phase on a miss. The final `evaluate`
step holds a static deliverable gate plus a reviewer QA pass. What it adds
over the generic `build-loop`: a specialist role per phase, a
domain-correct ordering, and a concrete per-phase quality bar.

Deliverables marked "artifact" land in the project's artifacts drawer (`write_artifact` / `read_artifact`), not the shipped workspace — review output is not product source.

Phases:

1. Outline the deck (planner) — narrative arc + per-slide bullets from the source → gated on artifact `{{workPath}}/outline.md` (markdown-notes)
2. Slide design (designer) — a consistent slide template + palette → gated on artifact `{{workPath}}/design-system.md` (markdown-notes)
3. Build the deck (developer) — generate the slides to the template → gated on `index.html` (slide-deck)

The gates never advance with an unmet criterion, and loop back to the
owning phase to fix named gaps.

workPath.title: Working folder
workPath.description: Per-task working folder in the artifacts drawer for this run's intermediate files. Defaults to this task's own folder so concurrent runs never overwrite each other; override with a stable name only when runs should deliberately share working files.

steps.name: Outline the deck
steps.description: narrative arc + per-slide bullets from the source
steps.prompt: Read every supplied source file with workspace `read_file` before outlining. Build a source-grounded deck plan: a title slide, a clear narrative arc, 5-7 content slides with one idea and 2-4 bullets each, and a takeaways/CTA ending. Attach a source filename or source heading to every factual claim. Write an **acceptance-criteria checklist** ("opens with a title slide", "one idea per slide", "ends with takeaways/CTA", "every claim traces to the source"). Save the outline + checklist to artifact `{{workPath}}/outline.md` with `write_artifact`; note the path in task notes.

steps.name: Slide design
steps.prompt: Read artifact `{{workPath}}/outline.md` with `read_artifact`. Design one reusable slide system: title position, body/grid layout, exact palette, type scale, spacing, progress affordance, and focused/inactive slide states. Include desktop and narrow-screen behavior plus keyboard/button navigation treatment. Consistency matters more than flourish. Save the template spec to artifact `{{workPath}}/design-system.md` with `write_artifact`; note the path in task notes. No slide content yet.

steps.name: Build the deck
steps.description: generate the slides to the template
steps.prompt: Read artifacts `{{workPath}}/outline.md` and `{{workPath}}/design-system.md` with `read_artifact`. Build the deck in workspace `index.html` with `write_file`: one semantic section per slide, inline CSS/JS, visible slide count/progress, previous/next controls, and ArrowLeft/ArrowRight keyboard navigation. Apply the template uniformly and use only claims in the outline/source. Keep it self-contained with no external assets. On a loop-back, fix only the named gaps. `write_task_note` the workspace path and slide count.

steps.name: Evaluate
steps.description: Grade the deliverable against every acceptance criterion. All pass → finish; any fail → loop back and fix the gap.
steps.prompt:
Read workspace `index.html` with `read_file` and artifacts `{{workPath}}/outline.md` and `{{workPath}}/design-system.md` with `read_artifact`. Check narrative flow (title opening, one idea per slide, takeaways ending), visual consistency, source fidelity, and both button and keyboard navigation. Render and exercise it if browser QA is available; otherwise trace the event handlers. Write PASS/FAIL per criterion.

Then record your verdict — this is the whole point of the loop:

1. If any criterion fails, first write the specific gaps to the task notes with `write_task_note`: which file, which part, and what is missing. The "Build the deck" step reads them when it fixes the work.
2. When you have graded every criterion, write `{{workPath}}/verdict.md` with `write_artifact`. One line per criterion and no preamble: the criterion, its one-line reason, then PASS or FAIL as the last word on the line. Writing verdict.md completes this step.

The runtime routes on the verdict: every line PASS moves the task to "Finish"; any FAIL sends it back to "Build the deck" to fix those gaps, and a review that keeps failing pauses the task for the user. Mark a criterion PASS only when it is met. The build phase's completion gate already blocked a grossly-incomplete deliverable; your job is the judgment an automated check cannot make (does it actually work, read well, look right).

checks.label: the verdict marks its criteria PASS

steps.name: Finish
steps.description: All acceptance criteria met. Stamp a short summary and report DONE.
steps.prompt: Every acceptance criterion passed. Write a one-paragraph DONE summary to task notes via `write_task_note`: what was built, the deliverable path(s), and a one-line confirmation that each criterion is met. Then report DONE.
